standard_prerequisites.name: Completeness for propositional logic
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a set of sentences is consistent then it is satisfiable; the unit proves this as its completeness theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: The first link runs the contrapositive: if Gamma is unsatisfiable it cannot be consistent (558-559).

standard_prerequisites.name: Soundness for propositional logic
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a set of sentences is satisfiable then it is consistent; the unit proves this as its soundness theorem.
standard_prerequisites.use: The contrapositive converts inconsistency into unsatisfiability, both for Gamma itself (558) and again for the finite subset Gamma_0 at the end of the chain (562-563).

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of derivations
standard_prerequisites.statement: A derivation is a finite tree of rule applications whose open assumptions form a finite set; hence if Gamma proves two contradictory sentences then some finite subset Gamma_0 of Gamma already proves both.
standard_prerequisites.use: This unpacks the middle link of the chain (559-561): inconsistency of Gamma means two derivations exist from Gamma, and the finitely many assumptions they use make up the finite subset Gamma_0 that is itself inconsistent.

core_obligations: Note the chain is read in the contrapositive: Gamma is unsatisfiable if and only if it is inconsistent, where the forward direction is the contrapositive of completeness and the backward direction is the contrapositive of soundness (558-559).

Unpack inconsistency of Gamma as the existence of derivations from Gamma of a sentence and of its negation, and use that each derivation has finitely many open assumptions: the union of those assumptions is a finite subset Gamma_0 of Gamma, and the same two derivations are derivations from Gamma_0, so Gamma_0 is inconsistent; conversely a derivation from a subset of Gamma is a derivation from Gamma (559-561).
Apply the unsatisfiability-implies-inconsistency direction again to the finite subset Gamma_0: since Gamma_0 is inconsistent it is unsatisfiable (562-563).
Assemble the four links to conclude that Gamma is unsatisfiable if and only if some finite subset Gamma_0 of Gamma is unsatisfiable, which is the contrapositive of the counted statement (514-519).

proof_roadmap.step: Trade unsatisfiability of Gamma for inconsistency through completeness and soundness.
Trade inconsistency of Gamma for inconsistency of a finite subset Gamma_0, using that derivations have finitely many open assumptions.
Trade inconsistency of Gamma_0 back for unsatisfiability, closing the chain.
Read the chain contrapositively to obtain the counted two-sided statement.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the Compactness Theorem for propositional logic at source lines 508-512: a set of sentences is satisfiable exactly when every finite subset is. The author proof (514-519) is a three-link chain of equivalences, and each link demands a different tool: satisfiability is traded for consistency through the completeness theorem and its converse through soundness, both proved earlier in the same unit, while the middle link trades consistency of an infinite set for consistency of a finite subset, which needs the structural fact that a derivation has finitely many open assumptions. None of the links is a definition unpacking alone, and the reader has to see which direction of which theorem each step uses, so the unit is more than a one-line consequence of the definitions.
